The estate can recover the losses that accrued before she died: the medical and ambulance costs, lost earnings up to death, and pain and suffering, plus any funeral costs paid. Whether the driver also pays for the death itself depends on whether a court treats her sincere religious refusal as reasonable (most common-law courts lean that way, so the driver is liable under the "take the victim as you find her" rule and dependants can claim loss of support in their own right) or as an unreasonable failure to mitigate that breaks causation (which would bar or reduce those death-related damages). This is contested and varies by jurisdiction.

CONFIDENCE: 55
